chapter: Music in the family, learning to play
title: Leon Kellner: substitute piano work, union advice, Biloxi offer
summary: Hirsch subbed for pianist Leon Kellner, advised him on union insurance, and was offered a Biloxi job.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Did you play with Kellner, Dan?

I said, I was, I was sort of, I was sort of Leon's godfather. Really? Whenever he needed a substitute, when he went to New York, I'd end up playing piano for him. And, uh, whenever he wanted to fire somebody, he'd have to ask me, how do you fire him? And we were very close. In fact, the last thing he asked me to do is how to, how to get out of, of, uh, get out of, uh, a losing proposition belonging to the New York local. And I told him I've got the same problem that we've been in so long that we pay for our life insurance. And if we get out now, we're going to lose it if we don't continue to pay for it. It's just like being a member of our local down here. That if you know, if you're, if you're, if you're a, if you're a honorary member that you were up until this last year, where you, you now have to pay dues. Mm-hmm. If you've already paid up your dues and paid your thousand dollars, if you, if you, if you de-met, well, you're out a thousand dollars in the event you're dying. You're, you're getting older all the time. There was a better chance for your family to get a thousand dollars. So I figured it out mathematically for Leon that if he paid his dues for the next twenty-four years and, and, and died, his, his state would get four hundred dollars.
But he had to die within so many years. But, uh, maybe he'd get a few projects or something.
You know, he's down in Florida now, you know. Yeah. I've heard that but I don't know where he is. I know where he is.
Is he still working at the Broadwater?
No. No. He's not at the Broadwater anymore. That's Mrs. Brown. That's sorts of Biloxi. No, he's down in Boca Raton, Florida, I think. Some friends of mine told me they saw him down there.

Yeah. There's no chicken anymore. Is he playing down there? Yeah. He's playing. He's a damn good piano player. Yeah. But he's quite a guy. We've always had good relations between us. In fact he wanted me to come over to Biloxi. He wanted to go up to New York for something, I don't remember who it was, and he offered me a job over in Biloxi. It was a very beneficent job, fifty dollars a night, and room and board. But I didn't think I could afford to, I think I eat more than fifty dollars a day. I told him I had other contracts that I had to fulfill and I didn't want to hurt his feelings. But he tried to get a piano player to get over there. I mean he's getting at least three or four hundred dollars a week, and he wanted to get rid of it for nothing. I don't need publicity anymore.
Not that kind of publicity, huh?
